prompt:
I have a side business buying limited-supply watches from stores overseas and reselling them in my country, where they’re much harder to get. I told my partner about a possible opportunity to buy 2 watches that each trade for roughly 5 figures over market value. I’ve been hunting these specific watches for months and this one deal would equal my yearly salary at my regular job.

My partner then asked if they could also buy one if I managed to get an extra. I said no, that I’d buy every watch I could because each one means 5 figures in profit for me. They got really upset and said I’d basically denied them half a year’s salary for no reason. I see it as me effectively gifting them that money if I gave up such a rare, hard-won opportunity. Our financial situations are very different, so it would impact them more.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My dad has had a gambling problem for most of my life and is terrible with money. When I was 7, he took my sister and me to a horse track. He gave us $500 each to bet. I picked a 99-to-1 horse and won a huge payout. When we got home, my mom was furious; that incident was the final straw and they divorced. 

My dad has drifted in and out of our lives since, while my mom raised us. She put that money into savings and low-risk investments for me. When I was 14, I decided half would be for me and half for my sister for college or something professional.

Two months ago my dad asked me for $25,000, saying he’d lost his job and would lose his house because of gambling debts. I refused, saying I wouldn’t risk our start-in-life money, especially after spending almost all my part-time job earnings on his therapy. He exploded, said it was his money and I was ungrateful. Some friends say I’m heartless.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My son has been with "Sarah" for four years in a very on-again/off-again relationship. I really can’t stand her, but when they seemed more serious this past year, I tried to bite my tongue.

At a big family dinner, including extended family and people she didn’t know, Sarah decided to propose to my son. She had my daughter’s girlfriend secretly video it, then stood up mid-dinner and sang a proposal. My son had his head in his hands and looked very upset, people were trying not to laugh, and it was painfully awkward. She then pulled out a ring she’d bought for herself and gave it to him to give back to her.

I went to check on dessert and laughed in the kitchen with my SIL. When I came back, I saw my husband and started laughing again; others were also laughing or trying not to. Later, Sarah told me I was rude and sexist. I told her it was her fault for doing it in front of a crowd.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I flew to another country for two days to visit a very sick relative. I asked a friend to drop me off and pick me up from the airport because I didn’t want to leave my new car there. I offered $150 up front for the rides (it’s about a 20‑minute round trip), bought her breakfast, and filled up her gas tank; she’s unemployed.

When I landed, she never showed. She ignored my calls and texts. After an hour, she finally messaged on Facebook saying she was taking a “mental health day” and that border questioning gives her anxiety, so she wouldn’t pick me up. I asked her to at least Venmo me half the money back; she refused, claimed she thought it was a gift because she’s broke, and told me to get an Uber or contact distant relatives. My uncle eventually drove a few hours to get me. Now she’s telling everyone I don’t care about her mental health and that I’m cheap for asking for my money back.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My young daughters are obsessed with YouTube personalities and have begged for their own channel for about a year. My partner and I have repeatedly told them no and tried to redirect them.

They recently came back from visiting my in‑laws and excitedly announced, “We have our own YouTube channel!” My brother‑in‑law and his wife went over our heads, created a non‑private channel, filmed them, and uploaded videos. The content is just them chatting in a spare bedroom, but the channel is under his control, not ours.

I’m furious and want to confront him about filming and managing a channel for our children without our consent and make it clear that if he does anything like this again, he’ll be cut off from them. My partner was initially angry too but has calmed down and thinks I should let it go since nothing bad has happened yet.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I hosted a Zoom dinner party with family and some friends. They’re very passionate about politics and argue intensely over the few things they disagree on. I wanted a fun night without debate or people feeling pressured to take sides, so in the invite I said everyone was welcome as long as they agreed not to bring up politics and to keep current events focused on their own lives rather than the news.

Most people were fine with this. During the event, someone abruptly brought up the election. I changed the topic back to movies, but they went back to the election. I gently reminded everyone we were avoiding politics for the night.

That guest said I was policing their speech, that it was privileged and entitled to just talk about movies while the world is collapsing and people are suffering, and that they felt obligated to speak out. Now I’m wondering if my “no politics” rule made me the problem.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My mom has been asking to have my son stay with her because she’s lonely since my dad died. My spouse and I refused because of what happened last time we left our son (he was 8 then) with her.

My mom has gotten deep into conspiracy theories. We left our son with her for a month while we went on a trip. When he went back to school, they were talking about 9/11 and he immediately said, “My grandma said the Zionist Jews did it.” His teacher called us asking what my mom was teaching him. We were embarrassed and I called my mom asking what she was telling my kid. She defended herself, insisting it was true and saying things like, “Do you know how many Jews died in 9/11? None!” I just hung up.

Because of that, we’re refusing to let her take care of him now. Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My neighbor has a few dogs, including a sheepdog. One day I was outside and he called me over, said he was having knee problems, and asked if I could walk his dogs. I agreed. He told me the leashes were in his shed. There were several on a table and one newer-looking one in the corner. I grabbed the clean one and some others, then got the dogs.

While walking them, the sheepdog suddenly tried to sprint across the road. When I pulled back, the leash failed and the dog went into the path of a car and died. My neighbor was upset but said that leash had never worked right, which is why it was in the corner. I apologized for not checking; he apologized for not noticing which leash I took.

This morning his daughter called, said the dog was hers and cost about $1,600, and asked me to pay. I refused. My partner says I’m responsible and should pay.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My mother is slowly dying of stage 4 cancer. After a brain hemorrhage, she can’t move much but can still talk, is sometimes confused but still herself. I don’t want to spend my whole day with her because she’s insufferable. She yells at me over small things in front of others. 

For example, I went to get her food from a restaurant about 20 minutes away, and with traffic and parking it took 40–50 minutes. When I came back, she yelled that I can’t do anything right. Another time, my father asked me a simple question and when I answered, she yelled that I’m selfish for talking to him and mocked me as “the princess.” She has always been hateful toward me. 

Visits are a 2-hour drive each way, I have finals, and being there hurts my mental health. I still visit for about an hour at a time, but my sister says I’ll regret not being there more and that I’m letting our mother die alone.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I lost both my parents in 2020. Before they died, they asked me to oversee the trusts they set up for my sister’s children and stepchildren. Each child is supposed to receive a lump sum at 20. My sister knows the money exists and that I’m in charge until they’re old enough.

Her first husband died years ago, and his family has stayed involved with her biological kids. At Christmas those kids learned they each have a large savings account funded by their late father and grandparents. It seems like a lot of money, and my sister and her current husband were rattled because this puts those kids far ahead of the stepkids, who never had that kind of extended family support.

My sister asked me to move her biological kids’ trust money into the stepkids’ trusts to even things out. I refused and said I’d follow our parents’ instructions and not change anything. She says I’m going to make the stepkids feel awful and further divide her family.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My husband recently brought home a puppy behind my back. I’m allergic to dogs and had repeatedly told him I can’t live with one because my allergies are severe. I told him he could get a cat, a chinchilla, or another animal I’m not allergic to, and I’d be fine with it.

He said he thought I was lying about my allergies and told me to just take allergy pills. Dog allergy medication doesn’t work for me; even with it, I can barely sleep and have difficulty breathing because I also have asthma.

I told a good friend about the situation, and he offered to take the dog because his daughter really wanted one. I had him pick up the dog while my husband was at work. I stay home with the kids and handle cooking and cleaning. When my husband came home and saw the dog was gone, he freaked out, we argued, he threatened to leave, and refused to eat dinner.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

About 7 months ago I adopted a kitten from my university’s shelter program. I share an apartment with my dad, and the cat is very attached to us. He was feral and only really trusts us.

My parents are divorced and live in different states. I’m staying with my dad because he’s close to my university; my younger brother lives with our mom. My brother is highly allergic to cats, as is my mom. Before I adopted the cat, my brother clearly said he never wanted to visit our father again because of our rough, abusive past with him.

When my mom heard about the cat, she flipped and told me to get rid of him because my brother “has to see his father.” Now my brother suddenly wants to visit because “dad has money,” and my mom is pressuring me again to rehome my cat so my brother can stay a weekend.

I’ve suggested allergy meds and planning activities away from the apartment so exposure is minimal. My mom says I’m choosing a cat over my brother.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My boyfriend and I have been dating for 7 months. We usually get takeout, but after I was promoted we went to a very nice Italian restaurant with a dress code to celebrate.

He’s not the nicest eater, but I didn’t realize he had no table manners. When our bruschetta appetizer came, he asked if I’d be upset if he ate like he does at home. I said we were at a nice restaurant with other customers. He then ignored the serving fork and started digging in with his hands, getting sauce all over his fingers. I let that go.

When the pasta came, he smirked and ate with his hands again, dropping his fork, grabbing chicken and noodles, getting sauce on the tablecloth, his clothes, and his face, then loudly burped. People stared, the waiter checked on him, and he put his feet on the chair next to us, blocking the aisle. I was mortified, paid the check, and left. He says it’s my fault for not letting him enjoy his meal.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I live in a house with four other housemates. One housemate is dating a girl I’ll call Emily. She has stayed at our place literally every day for two months, using our utilities, eating our groceries without asking, doing her laundry there even though she has her own apartment, using our stuff, going into our rooms without permission, and bringing her friends over.

Last Friday she brought friends over to cook without telling anyone. Someone broke a glass and left shards all over the counter. Another housemate cut his finger the next morning. I confronted her and she denied it, implied it was me, then reluctantly agreed to clean. She did a bad job and I later cut my foot on glass; another housemate had glass fly out of the disposal.

We had a house meeting where I yelled at her about the lying and disrespect and told her she couldn’t stay more than half the week. She cried, and her boyfriend says I was too harsh.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I live with two roommates. One roommate works from home and does laundry constantly, like 4–6 times a week. We tried assigning laundry days, but she demanded four days and both weekend days, leaving only three days for me and the other roommate, so we went back to first come, first serve.

One Sunday I put my laundry in at 6 a.m. and set an alarm for 10 a.m. to move it. When I went back, she had taken my wet clothes out of the washer, put them on top of the dryer, and run her own load. I had wool items in there that got ruined, and I had to throw some away.

When I tried to talk to her, she wouldn’t admit any fault, said I was stealing the washer and dryer from her, and accused me of hogging the laundry room. The appliances are mine, so I disconnected them and told her she couldn’t use them. She’s furious and telling people I had no right.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I’m the youngest of three brothers. Our mom died when we were kids, and our dad remarried Janet, who has two disabled children. We told him it felt too fast, but he said it was best for all of us. After the marriage, my brothers and I lost a lot: we had to adjust our needs for her kids, missed out on things because they needed full-time care, had less money, and got less time with our dad and extended family.

Now we’re all adults and out of the house. None of us really talks to our dad anymore; we feel we lost him when he remarried. Dad and Janet are now asking us to commit to caring for her kids after they both die, since there’s no other family willing to step in. All three of us said no. Dad is guilt-tripping me, saying I’m a good person and it’s wrong to leave vulnerable people without family. I still don’t want to agree.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My husband's friend is getting married abroad by the beach. I booked our flights and accommodation as soon as we got the date because I was excited and wanted a good place before options ran out. I recently lost a lot of weight and have a lot of loose skin, and I’m not comfortable with anyone but my husband seeing my body. I didn’t want a hotel with a shared pool, so I booked a 3‑bedroom villa with a private pool (the smallest available). 

My husband told his friend about the good deal. Later, he and his fiancée asked us to stay somewhere else and let some of her family use the villa, offering to refund what we paid. Now there are no similar villas left; hotels cost about the same, and I couldn’t use their pools. I refused and explained why. She called me selfish for “hogging” a 3‑bedroom place. My husband thinks I should give it up for their special day.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My sister went through a horrible divorce and lost her home, so I let her live with me for two years so she could save money. I’m a single parent of two girls, 9 and 4. She helps around the house, pays some bills, and babysits while I work, which saved me daycare costs. 

The problem is she started overstepping. She wanted to come to school events and then began introducing my kids as her own. I told her that was confusing and she stopped briefly, but then I found out my new neighbors think she’s their mom. 

Yesterday my youngest called her “mommy” in front of me. My older daughter later told me my sister told them to call her “mommy” in public and they were scared to tell me. I confronted my sister and, during the argument, I snapped and told her if she wants kids so much she should adopt some of her own, even though I know she can’t have children. My family says I was cruel.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

Two years ago my sister was pregnant with a baby girl after a previous miscarriage. Because of that, she told only our immediate family and asked us to wait before making any public announcement. Our mom went ahead and posted the pregnancy on Facebook anyway. My sister only found out from the flood of congratulations texts and was devastated. She didn’t speak to our mom for a long time, and our mom never apologized, saying it was her news too since she was becoming a grandma.

Earlier, when my brother told the family he had eloped, she told him he made the family look “classless” and asked what her friends were supposed to think.

Later, my partner and I were expecting a baby. Remembering all this, I deliberately did not tell my mom before we made our own public announcement. When she saw it on Facebook, she called screaming that we were selfish. Now extended family keeps telling me I should apologize, but I refuse.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I work in a large room where no one is allowed to use headphones, so we have a shared speaker. At first everyone took turns and played a mix of music. Then my coworker Samantha started coming in earlier than everyone else and using the speaker every single day. When her music is on, it’s either very vulgar rap (including WAP, which once played while I was trying to talk to a manager) or music in a language only she understands. She says that’s all she likes.

All of us, including managers, have talked to her about compromising, but she just rolls her eyes or improves for one day then goes back to the same thing. We don’t want to push management too hard and lose music altogether.

As a taste of her own medicine, I came in before her one day and played nothing but 70s, 80s, and 90s country all day on the shared speaker to show what it’s like to be forced to listen to music you dislike.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My best friend had a destination wedding and I was maid of honor. My partner of 5+ years took time off work and we got a hotel for two nights. I did all my maid of honor duties: bought the dress she wanted, threw the bachelorette party, stood next to her in church, gave a speech, etc.

At the reception there was one long table. My seat was right next to the bride, but my partner was at the far end, next to the photographer and a family who didn’t speak his language. The best man had his wife seated right next to him. I suspect my friend seated my partner that way because we’re not married and she’s very religious.

I could tell my partner felt hurt. After the food was served, I left my seat by the bride and went to sit in the empty seat next to my partner. Later another friend said it was shitty to leave my place of honor.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I started working from home two months ago. My husband bought our small house before we got together and always calls it his property. It has two rooms; one was empty until I began using it as my office.

Everything was fine until he sat me down and said he expects 30% of my income as “profit” because he provides the office. I was shocked. He said it’s his house and he could use the room for himself. I refused and called him unreasonable. We argued, and I told him he wouldn’t get a penny. He accused me of taking advantage, even though there’s no mortgage. I do all the chores and pay half the bills.

He involved his family. His mom says I’m being difficult, that 30% isn’t much, and that the room gives me stability so he should benefit.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

During a shift at a department store where we’re allowed to stop shoplifters and must charge them for the full value taken, a woman came in with a toddler in a stroller. She went straight to cosmetics, put several very expensive perfumes in the stroller, and covered them with the toddler’s blanket. Then she went to children’s clothing and hid a couple of items under the same blanket.

When we approached her, she started crying and said she was only stealing the clothing. I pulled back the blanket and revealed the perfume, and she then said she was a single mother and begged us to work with her. We took her to the office and the total was just over the felony threshold. Policy doesn’t allow altering the amount, so I stepped out and called the police.

No one could come for the child, so we waited for a social worker. She was arrested and is trying to make bail, and I feel awful.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I was at a rock concert in the mosh pit, just enjoying myself. I bumped into someone in a wheelchair, raised my hand in apology, and went back to vibing. After the artist finished, there was about a 20-minute gap before the next act.

The person in the wheelchair came up to me and started berating me for “blatantly trampling them.” I apologized, but I didn’t really mean it because in a mosh pit you get thrown around and can’t control where you go. They kept going, so I said, “Well maybe the mosh pit isn’t for you then.” They called me a bigot, and I just said, “Cool, whatever, I’m going to get a drink. Next act is on in 20 if you wanna take on the pit again.”

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

While boarding a plane, I got to my row and saw someone already sitting in the aisle seat where I had the window seat. I said, “Hey, I’m in the window seat here,” assuming he’d just get up so I could sit down. Instead, he looked at me, ignored the long line of people waiting behind us, and said, “What’s the magic word?”

I stared at him and replied, “We’re not doing this right now.” That really pissed him off. He stood up but gave me an earful while moving, and he kept ranting for the rest of the flight about “entitled millennials.” My friends say I should’ve just said “please.”

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My close friend hates being surprised and has always said they don’t like surprise parties or big surprise gestures. Their partner told me he was planning an elaborate proposal during a day trip with dinner and a park proposal. 

Next time I saw my friend, I immediately told them about the plan. They were happy because they want to marry him, and I told them to act surprised and not let on that they knew. Later, my friend slipped and revealed she knew. Her boyfriend confronted me, we argued, and I told him he should have considered that she hates surprises.

Later my friend told me I’m not invited to the wedding because of the argument. I called her boyfriend to talk; he still refused to invite me, so I called him a massive prick for driving a wedge between me and my friend.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My partner and I have been planning for Halloween. My partner wants us to go together to a few parties and clubs, wearing a very revealing Princess Jasmine costume: basically a blue bra and very transparent, loose pants. I’m a big Aladdin fan and actually played Aladdin in a school play, so at first I was really touched by the Jasmine idea. But I’m not comfortable with such a “sexy” costume.

I asked my partner not to wear it. My partner was upset, said this is the outfit they want and that they’ll wear it whether I agree or not. I do understand it’s their body and their choice, but I feel really uncomfortable with my partner going to multiple parties and bars dressed like that, with lots of drinking and everyone in sexy outfits. I’ve said if they wear it, I might not go with them.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My 15‑year‑old son is very social and usually talks to me about school and problems. My husband feels our son favors me and has tried to bond over fishing and hunting, which our son hates, leading to fights about him being “forced” to like those things.

Recently our son became very quiet and sad and wouldn’t tell me why. My husband was looking for something in his room and found a diary. I told him to put it back, but he said it wouldn’t hurt to look for an explanation. I was worried too, so I let him read it. We discovered something big that explained his behavior. I told my husband not to say anything.

He ignored me and brought it up, trying to “help.” Our son exploded, called us horrible parents, took the diary, and is now cold and distant with both of us, especially me, despite my attempts to apologize and comfort him.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I’ve been with my boyfriend for almost two years. We’re very open with our phones; we often scroll with the other able to see everything, and there’s never been anything secret.

Yesterday he got a message from a friend while we were watching a movie. I offered to pause so he could reply, but he said he’d wait because they were talking about things his friend was going through. I asked what, and he said he wasn’t comfortable sharing things people had confided in him. I was weirded out because in past relationships, we always shared this kind of stuff, and he once told me I could share similar things with him because he’s my partner.

I told him it felt strange that he wouldn’t tell me, especially since I always share when he asks. He said I don’t have a right to know everything and not to make it about me. We didn’t fight, but it dampened the evening.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

On my way to the gym I often saw a small female dog that looked miserable. Her owner is a homeless man who sometimes is with her, but often leaves her tied to a pole for hours. I thought about reporting it, but was told most local shelters are kill shelters, which might be worse.

It’s been snowing a lot recently, and seeing her tied up again was too much. One night my fiancé and I walked by, saw the dog alone, and decided to take her home. My mother was outraged, saying homeless people need their animals for companionship and I had no right. I argued that a dog isn’t a toy and you shouldn’t have one you can’t care for.

We took the dog to a vet: she’s a bit over a year old and malnourished but not critical. We’ve reported her as abandoned so we can adopt her or have my aunt’s family do it after the legal wait.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I'm hosting Christmas dinner this year with our usual menu that everyone knows. My sister-in-law’s kids, who are 6 and 9, are extremely picky eaters. She called to inform me she’d be bringing separate food for them because she said there’s nothing on my menu they would eat. 

I told her I was sorry but there wouldn’t be enough space at the table for extra meals and that the kids should start learning to tolerate some foods, especially at a family holiday where it’s expected to eat what’s served without complaining. I suggested it’s a passing phase and one dinner wouldn’t hurt. She insisted she doesn’t want them hungry or snacking all night. I apologized and still declined.

My husband says I’m being inconsiderate and that I lose nothing by allowing it. His sister is now reconsidering coming and says I’m ruining the celebration.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My wife and I have three daughters (15, 13, and 10). We vacationed with my siblings, their spouses, and their kids. The rental had a big bunkroom for all the girls: two bunk beds with trundles and a single bed. My youngest is very sick and physically can’t manage a top bunk or a trundle, so she needed a bottom bunk or the single. My siblings agreed beforehand.

When we arrived, the girls rushed in and claimed beds oldest to youngest, like usual, and my youngest was left with a top bunk. No one would switch, including my older daughters. I put my youngest in my room instead. The next day she came to us crying because her cousins were teasing her for sleeping with her parents. My older daughters didn’t defend her and said she was old enough to defend herself.

She was miserable, so we ended the trip early and went home. My older two were furious and said she was spoiled, and my siblings said I ruined the vacation over this.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My parents live abroad and bought plane tickets for me and my sister to visit them for their anniversary. My sister has two kids, a 6‑month‑old and a 5‑year‑old, and the flight was about 10 hours. About a week before the trip, she called and asked if I’d help her take care of the kids on the flight, talking about taking shifts so we could both sleep. I told her I wasn’t comfortable with that. She brushed it off, said my nephew loves me and we’d work something out on the flight, then hung up.

I was annoyed and upgraded my ticket to business class using points plus $50 so I could sleep and avoid babysitting. At the airport I told her I’d upgraded, and she was clearly unhappy and now sends me guilt‑trippy messages about family. She has a history of dumping her kids on me, and on this trip I still ended up babysitting while she went sightseeing.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I’ve been with my girlfriend for two years. She’s in film school and made a short film for class that the school funded. She wrote it, directed it, and stars as the main character. There’s going to be a screening at her school with about 150 students and faculty, and she wants me to go as her date.

I’m proud of her, but I really don’t want to see it because there’s a topless scene with her (in a medical, nonsexual context) and a love scene with another guy. I understand it’s acting and “art,” but I hate the idea of being in a room full of people watching my girlfriend topless and in a sex scene. I was already uncomfortable knowing it was filmed at all.

I told her I might not be able to watch it, and she got upset and called me selfish and insecure. I’m considering just going and trying to endure it, but I’m worried how I’ll feel. Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

When I walk my dog, I always pick up the poop and carry the bag until I reach a trash can. I use either public city cans at intersections or the wheeled cans people leave by the street. The cans say “property of city of X” and are required for city trash service. Many neighbors leave them on the strip between sidewalk and street all week.

I only use cans that are on the street or reachable from the sidewalk; I never go onto private property. I tie the bags tightly to reduce odor. If someone used my can for dog poop, I wouldn’t care, though I usually keep my cans in back so they aren’t accessible.

My boyfriend says I’m wrong because it stinks up people’s cans and it’s technically illegal to dump trash in them without permission. I think if they don’t want that, they should move the cans off the street.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My daughter Rose (9) is a very advanced reader. She’s in 3rd grade but reads at about a 9th grade level. Despite that, the only books she wants to read are the I Survived series and A-Z Mysteries, which are far below her level.

I told her it’s fine to read those at school, but at home she has to read things closer to her level. I’ve taken her to bookstores and tried the young adult section, but she says those books are boring and gross. She keeps asking for books from the children’s section and I keep saying no because they’re too easy.

She started sneaking books home from school, and when I took those away, she stopped reading altogether and pulled away from me. Her teacher recommends I let her read whatever she wants. Her dad is angry with me and says I’m wrong.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

I have a very good relationship with my mom, unlike my wife. My siblings can usually afford pricey gifts for her, so this year I decided to finally get her something nice and expensive for Christmas. I bought a $600 necklace for my mom using our joint account, which my wife mainly funds and uses to pay our bills and rent.

When my wife found out, she went off on me, saying I should’ve told her and that I shouldn’t have taken that much from the account, especially now that we’re struggling. My best friend and I always prank each other. Before his recent wedding, I told my girlfriend that all the women had been asked to wear white as a quirky thing the bride and groom were doing. She was reluctant, but I insisted it was expected, so she bought a white dress.

When we arrived, everyone else was in normal wedding attire. My girlfriend was mortified. My best friend laughed and joked that it looked like we were the ones getting married. Now I feel really bad. I honestly didn’t think it would be such a big deal and feel like it’s being blown out of proportion, but I’m not sure.

I have four kids, but this is about my 10-year-old son Jack and 8-year-old son Tony. They were playing Mario Kart on their 3DSs. Jack knows he’s supposed to let Tony win, because if Tony loses he throws a tantrum. Tony’s 3DS needed charging, so they swapped devices.

This time Jack didn’t let Tony win. Tony threw his usual tantrum and hurled Jack’s 3DS across the room, breaking it badly. Jack was very upset. I got mad at Jack, because he’s been told repeatedly to let Tony win to avoid tantrums.

My husband and my two daughters (16 and 17) think I should make Tony give Jack his 3DS, but I believe it’s Jack’s fault for handing over his device and then not letting Tony come in first. Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My 8-year-old had a parent-teacher conference where the teacher said he has good grades but shouts and acts up in class. Afterward, he wanted to buy a book at the school book fair. My wife hesitated, and I firmly said no. He got huffy, said he was going in anyway, and ran into the library. We told him we were leaving and walked out; he knew we were going to the car.

I put our three younger kids in the car. My wife took them home, assuming I was going back in to get him. Instead, I stayed in the car in direct view of the school exit, intending to teach him a lesson. About 20 minutes later he came out, panicking and crying, thinking we had left him.

My wife is angry that I didn’t go in to get him and that I let him believe we had left him there. Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

When I was 12, my dad ran off with my mom's friend. My parents never legally divorced. My mom passed away a few years ago, and my dad passed away late last year.

I already got a good chunk from my mom, and I'm financially secure and do not need this money at all. I decided to contest the will so I would get everything instead of his girlfriend. My husband is losing mobility and doctors think it might be the start of a motor neuron disease. He has trouble walking and has lost sensation on one side of his torso, but we’re still months away from a firm diagnosis and our doctor told us not to immediately assume it’s a lifelong illness.

In the meantime, my husband wants to get a wheelchair and make our home wheelchair accessible. This house was bought for me by my parents before we got married; I lived here years before he moved in, and although it’s legally ours now, I still feel like it’s mine. I don’t want to install ramps or redo stairs because I’m worried it will hurt the house’s value and be expensive to undo later. I also think it’s too soon and want to wait a few months, but he wants to start now.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My best friend recently had a small wedding on a tight budget and asked me to bake her wedding cake as my gift. I made two identical cakes after seeing a prank video where someone pretends to trip and destroy the cake. I asked my brother to fake a fall with one of the cakes; he agreed. 

At the reception, my brother walked the first cake to the sweetheart table, pretended to trip, and fell on it. My friend immediately burst into tears and wouldn’t calm down. We yelled “gotcha!” and explained it was a joke, but my friend yelled that I ruined her wedding. Now she and her family are mad and she refuses to talk to me. Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

My baby is now 15 months old and has always been very hairy, with hair on the head, really full eyelashes, and over the last 4–5 months a fairly prominent unibrow. For purely aesthetic reasons, I decided to pluck the middle while my baby slept, planning to stop if my baby woke up. I managed to get it all off over a couple of days.

I didn’t think it was a bad thing. A friend with a child came over for a play date and, being very observant, noticed my baby’s eyebrows. I was honest and said I plucked the middle while my baby slept. She looked horrified and said she was surprised I did that. I didn’t know what to say and felt insecure about my decision.

My partner says I’m overthinking this, but I’m second-guessing myself now.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

During a tornado warning, our upstairs neighbor knocked and asked if he, his girlfriend, and their dog could shelter in our basement. We live in a duplex in an old house that’s been split into two units; they have the upper floors and we have the first floor and basement. I told him I wasn’t comfortable with them coming into our place and apologized. He stood there awkwardly for a moment, then left.

I felt that I’m not obligated to let people into my home just because there’s a storm. There wasn’t a tornado in the end and the sirens stopped about five minutes after he asked. Later, my partner told me I was being selfish, but I don’t think they should have access to our home every time there’s a storm warning.

Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".

When I told my daughter, she burst into tears, saying she’d never see her friends again. She and my husband are both angry and say we didn’t discuss it enough and that this won’t really solve the problem. I’ve started to feel guilty. Was I in the wrong? Respond only with "Yes" or "No".
